faqs.question: Who can sign in to the platform?
faqs.answer: Startups accepted into ODTÜ Teknokent programs, and the mentors, trainers and coordinators invited by the program team, can sign in. Registration is not open to everyone; you sign in with the role you were invited to.

faqs.question: How do I find my mentor?
faqs.answer: When you share the topic you want support on and the problem you face, you see mentor suggestions based on expertise, startup stage and availability. Each suggestion comes with a short reason explaining why it fits you.

faqs.question: How can I join a program?
faqs.answer: Program applications are shared in the Announcements section during application periods. When your application is accepted, an invitation is sent to your email so you can sign in.

faqs.question: What is the difference between training and mentoring?
faqs.answer: Mentoring is one-to-one or small-team meetings shaped by your startup's current situation and focused on decisions. Training is structured content designed to build knowledge and skills on a topic. If you have a specific problem, mentoring fits better; if you want to learn a topic from scratch, training does.

faqs.question: Can I take part in more than one program?
faqs.answer: That depends on each program's participation requirements. You can learn whether you can join more than one program in the same period from the program's requirements or the program team.

faqs.question: How are mentorship meetings scheduled?
faqs.answer: Meetings are scheduled from the mentor's available times. Each meeting comes with an agenda, the notes of the previous meeting and the items to finish beforehand, so both sides arrive prepared.

faqs.question: I can't find my invitation email. What should I do?
faqs.answer: First check your spam and promotions folders. If you still can't find it, contact your program's coordinator and ask them to send the invitation again.

faqs.question: Who can see my information on the platform?
faqs.answer: Meeting notes, task details and the documents you share are only visible to you and your mentor. Program management does not see the content; it only sees summary indicators such as how often you meet and how many tasks are completed.
